newsitem.title: UK: Fund calls on UK to seize Europe pension market.
newsitem.headline: Fund calls on UK to seize Europe pension market.

text.p: A UK pension fund manager has called on the country and the industry to seize the opportunity presented by under-funded pension schemes in Europe highlighted by a UK parliamentary committee report this week.

Marc Hommel, international pensions expert and director of Liberty International Pensions, said the crisis of outstanding pension liabilities in Continental Europe presented a huge opportunity for British pensions consultants and managers.
A report from parliament's Social Security committee released on Thursday drew attention to drastic underfunding of pension schemes in France, Italy, Spain and Germany.
"The issues raised...require tough measures by European governments, which could benefit the UK pensions industry," Hommel said.

"In particular there are tremendous opportunities for the UK fund management and insurance industries to manage the assets arising out of the increased funding of private provision required." He said the general move was away from final salary company pensions towards money purchase schemes. "Again the UK leads the way and could play an instrumental role in addressing the continental challenges."

The parliamentary report also called on the British government to pressure the European Commission to take pensions liabilities into account when calculating national debt -- part of key selection criteria for the first round of EMU.

Hommel agreed with a statement from the European Commission, -- trying to calm fears that Britain would be landed with the bill for other countries' pensions -- that Britain would not be liable under current arrangements.

But he said a Britain locked in to economic and monetary union could well suffer from "the relatively increased uncompetitiveness of (other) European countries as they grapple with the underfunding problem."
